rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ The relation $\gamma = 3\alpha$ holds for all materials including liquids. ✅ It holds only for ISOTROPIC SOLIDS. Liquids only have $\gamma$ — they have no $\alpha$ or $\beta$ because they have no fixed shape.  ·  ❌ A hole in a metal plate gets smaller when heated. ✅ The hole EXPANDS. The material around it moves outward equally in all directions, so the hole gets larger.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: ❌ $\alpha$, $\beta$, and $\gamma$ have different units. ✅ All three have the same units: K⁻¹ or °C⁻¹. They differ only in numerical value for isotropic solids ($\beta = 2\alpha$, $\gamma = 3\alpha$).  ·  ❌ The expansion ratios $\beta = 2\alpha$ and $\gamma = 3\alpha$ are exact for all temperature ranges. ✅ They are approximations valid when $\alpha\Delta T \ll 1$. For large $\Delta T$, higher-order terms become significant.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: The relation $\gamma = 3\alpha$ was first derived rigorously by James Clerk Maxwell in his 1871 theory of heat. It follows from the geometry of three-dimensional expansion.  ·  The anomalous expansion of water (maximum density at 4°C) means that ice floats and aquatic life survives winter. Without this anomaly, lakes would freeze from the bottom up, devastating ecosystems.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: **Superficial (area) expansion:** When a solid sheet is heated, its area increases. $\Delta A = A_0 \beta \Delta T$, where $\beta$ is the coefficient of superficial expansion.  ·  **Cubical (volume) expansion:** When a solid is heated, its volume increases. $\Delta V = V_0 \gamma \Delta T$, where $\gamma$ is the coefficient of cubical expansion.  ·  **Relation for isotropic solids:** $\alpha : \beta : \gamma = 1 : 2 : 3$. That is, $\beta = 2\alpha$ and $\gamma = 3\alpha$. This holds for isotropic materials (same properties in all directions).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ Only solids expand when heated — liquids and gases do not. ✅ Liquids and gases expand significantly more than solids. Mercury in a thermometer rises because liquid expansion is much larger than glass expansion.  ·  ❌ The volume of a cavity inside a solid does not change when heated. ✅ The cavity expands exactly as if it were filled with the solid material.
